target_customer: Small software and web development teams that wanted to plan work and show a public roadmap to clients and stakeholders
problem: Developers were constantly asked about progress. Interstate let them plot tasks as roads and routes and publicly share part or all of a roadmap.
business_model: Freemium SaaS: free for up to two users, then 9 dollars per extra user (version 2, June 2012)
product_category: Product roadmap and project management software

founders.name: Greg Cooper
founders.background_notes: Named as a founder by YC and TechCrunch (July 2011). No bio found.

founders.name: Simon Fletcher
founders.background_notes: Named as a founder by YC and TechCrunch. VentureBeat described the pair as UK-based.

exit.reason: Not public. YC marks the company Inactive, but no shutdown notice was found.

competitors.name: Basecamp (37signals)
competitors.what: Project management tool described as fairly basic

competitors.name: Pivotal Tracker
competitors.what: Agile tracker for developers, described as feature-heavy

competitors.name: Asana
competitors.what: Work management tool in private beta at the time

competitors.name: Flow (MetaLab)
competitors.what: General task management tool not aimed at developers

technical_complexity.rationale: A web app with task tracking, timelines, embeds and an API, built by two people. Standard CRUD with some front end polish.

defensibility.rationale: The public roadmap embed was a small feature on top of a crowded category and was easy for Basecamp, Asana or others to add.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Well funded tools kept growing. No acquisition or copy of Interstate specifically was found.

market_need_then: Developers wanted lighter project tools than Basecamp or Pivotal Tracker and wanted to show progress to clients. Launch named customers DailyBooth, Seesmic, Media Temple, Virginia Tech and Michigan Tech (TechCrunch, July 2011). A June 2012 TechCrunch article reports about 8,000 users in the body, conflicting with 200 in its metadata.

branding.domain_note: interstateapp.com used a suffix because interstate.com was not available to them (not sourced); it now redirects to an Atom.com name sale page.

identity.visual_style: Highway metaphor: tasks are Roads grouped into Routes (TechCrunch, July 2011)

branding.brand_signature: The road and route metaphor in the product vocabulary
branding.community_and_virality: Covered by TNW in September 2010 (4 out of 5 review) and TechCrunch in 2011 and 2012. No merch or community found.

brand_strength.rationale: A memorable metaphor but a very generic name that collides with highways, ELD apps and later unrelated startups, so it was hard to search for.

pivots.to: Freemium project management tool with chat and embeds (version 2)
pivots.why: TechCrunch reports version 2 added paid accounts, real-time chat and embeds to replace tools such as HipChat for small teams.

outcome_analysis: Interstate launched at YC Summer 2011 Demo Day as a roadmap tool for developers and went freemium with chat in June 2012. It never announced significant funding beyond the YC investment and is now marked Inactive. No source states when or why it stopped, so the cause is not public and no failure factor is assigned. The category held strong incumbents such as Basecamp and Asana.
notes: The 20,000 dollar seed with YC and Steve Blank rests on a single database (CB Insights); VentureBeat said the team was still seeking funding at launch. The founded year is unknown (TNW reviewed the product in September 2010, so it predates the batch). The domain_note guess about interstate.com is not sourced and should be treated as unknown. Website is dead (domain for sale). The YC page says the product comes from BakedCode. TechCrunch 2012 user numbers conflict (8,000 versus 200).
